prompt:
I need the front end for Pressbook Herbarium Kiosk. A touch kiosk in the lobby of a university natural history building that lets visitors, students and staff browse the herbarium's digitized plant specimens and pull up any single sheet in detail.

Who's using it: A group of four undergraduates in Field Botany (BOT 340) clustered around the kiosk between classes, led by Priya, who has used it once before. Their TA, Ben, is standing behind them, and a retired volunteer curator, Harold, drifts over to help. None of them has a collection login; the kiosk is open to anyone.

What they're doing right now: The class is doing a project on the native wildflowers of Coyote Hollow, the county preserve where they'll spend next Saturday. Priya wants to find every specimen of the genus Penstemon collected in the county, narrow it down to ones collected within about ten miles of the preserve in spring, and compare how the earliest and most recent collections look. She also wants to find out whether anyone ever collected Penstemon rattanii there. The others keep suggesting different filters at the same time, and when they find the 1938 sheet Harold remembers, they want to look at it closely together, including the handwritten label.

What's in the system at this point: Digitized collection: 41,860 specimen sheets, of which 312 are Penstemon (14 species) and 47 come from Lane County. Each specimen: catalog number (e.g., 'OSU-V-118204'), scientific name and determination history (some re-identified, e.g., 'det. as P. serrulatus 1938, annotated P. cardwellii 1991'), collector and collector number ('L. E. Detling 2216'), collection date, locality text ('rocky slope above Coyote Cr., 1,200 ft'), georeference with uncertainty radius, county, habitat notes, phenology (flowering/fruiting), high-resolution sheet image with label close-up, and condition notes. Date range of Lane County Penstemon: 1898–2019. 3 sheets currently on loan to another institution and not imaged. Featured exhibit this month: 'Pressed in Place: 125 Years of Oregon Collectors'. Kiosk resets to its welcome state after 3 minutes of no activity.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
